test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Under Section 25(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what may the Court do when a person is convicted in one trial for multiple offences?

options.text: Can impose only one punishment for all the offences, regardless of their nature
Must give the harshest punishment only and remit other punishments altogether
Shall suspend all sentences unless directed by a higher court in the same trial
May impose punishments to run either concurrently or consecutively as appropriate

solution:
The correct answer is __**May impose punishments to run either concurrently or consecutively as appropriate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Section 25(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 provides discretion to the Court when multiple offences are tried in a single trial.
 
• The Court can decide whether the punishments for multiple offences should run **concurrently (at the same time)** or **consecutively (one after another)**, based on the circumstances of the case.
 
• This ensures that the sentencing is proportional and tailored to the nature and gravity of the offences committed.
 
• The provision seeks to balance the principles of justice and deterrence while preventing excessive or overlapping punishments.
 
• The discretion under this section aligns with practices in criminal jurisprudence to uphold fairness in sentencing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concurrent Sentences:**

 
 
• When sentences run concurrently, the convict serves time for multiple offences simultaneously.
 
• This method is typically applied for related or less severe offences.
 
 
 
• **Consecutive Sentences:**
 
 
• When sentences run consecutively, the convict serves time for one offence after completing the sentence for another.
 
• This method is usually applied for unrelated or more severe offences.
 
 
 
• **Principles of Sentencing:**
 
 
• Sentencing aims to achieve deterrence, retribution, rehabilitation, and societal protection.
 
• The proportionality principle ensures that the punishment fits the gravity of the crime.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Discretion:**
 
 
• Judges have discretion under the law to interpret and apply sentencing provisions based on case facts.
 
• Discretion is guided by precedents, legal principles, and legislative intent.
